Sr. A. Serafina will join the community as vice-superior and alms-collector; she commends her to her. She writes nothing about the house, since she is about to go to Rome; on her return she will visit her.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Good Superior

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. The Delegate of S. P. d'Arena will send you Sr. A. Serafina; present her to the sisters as Vice-Delegate; she will take Sr. A. Ermelinda with her when she goes collecting alms.1 Never change her; for now she will account only to me for the money she receives; never ask her for any of it, except a little in extreme need.

  2. She will bring her camp bed, mattress, pillow and blanket; if you could put her in your room, at the foot of your bed, I would be pleased, if there is room.2

  3. You will have received my letter announcing my departure for Rome, so it is pointless to discuss everything now. On my return I shall come there and everything will be arranged; meanwhile ask around whether you could have a small flat from some benefactress.3

  4. I do [not] stop writing and appealing to my friends, and let us hope God will move some good heart for us; then I will write a letter to Sr. A. Serafina for the Marchioness Santi,4 and let us hope she will do something, as she has already shown she can.

5. Goodbye; everything you have done is fine; wait a few more days before calling the doctor; rub her with oil and camomile and then wrap her in the cloth, making sure it has been heated in the frying pan.5 Make a novena to the Eternal Father, trust in him, and she will be healed.

Goodbye, the Lord bless you; I am your

Mother Rosa G.

P.S. Never send Sr. A. Serafina to sit up at night; you may only send her on checking visits,6 never to nursing, because she suffers and falls ill.

1 Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi was being transferred from Sampierdarena to Genoa as vice-superior and alms-collector.

2 The Sister was in delicate health, so she asks her to have her sleep in her room, placing the bed, if possible, at the foot of her own.

3 They were still guests of Signora Caterina Rusca, whose house was not suitable for the community.

4 The Marchioness Santi; nothing more is known.

5 It is not known who the sick Sister was for whom she recommended rubs with oil and camomile.

6 Visits to the sick nursed by the Sisters to check how the service was going.

She tells her to open the letters addressed to her and send on only those she must answer personally. If the printer has printed the prayers composed by the Father, she should send some. For running the house and accepting girls and postulants, she should pray and then act as she thinks best.

[Our daughter]

  1. A line to tell you two small things: first, you must open and read all letters addressed to the house and then lock them away, because in the one you sent me you enclosed a certificate: it was Count Gazzola recommending Maddalena; those you see need an answer from me, send them on.2

  2. Now see whether the printer has got ready a few of the prayers the Father wrote; send them at once.

  3. As for the little girl you mention, do whatever you think right; take whom you like, and the same for the postulants; pray, and then go ahead, and God will be with you.

  4. Write to Sr. A. Serafina to keep the letter and take it herself when the lady returns from the country; and tell Maria that the Father is in Rome.3 I can't understand Fr. Luigi; I have seen nothing yet.

I am your poor

Mother Rosa

1 This autograph letter is written on Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino's letter dated 31 May 1871.

2 The certificates were parish priests' letters recommending sick people needing nursing or girls to be taken into the Institute. Count Giuseppe Gazzola was a priest in Piacenza.

3 Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi was in charge of collecting alms in Genoa; she was to deliver a letter to a lady to obtain a donation. Maria d'Annenkoff. Cf. L 44, n. 9.

She has been in Rome five days but has done and obtained nothing. Much prayer is needed to move the hearts of good people to help the Work of Saint Anne. Only Jesus can do it. She addresses a fervent prayer to him for the Daughters of Saint Anne, true Daughters of the Eternal Father. She always keeps them in mind and commends them to God.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. Today I received your letter telling me about Sr. A. Fortunata and the Parish Priest.1 Let us bless the Lord, who knows so well how to beautify the poor deeds of the Daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate.

  2. My daughter, this is already the fifth day I have been in this holy City and I have done nothing yet, obtained nothing.2 Let us pray; yes, pray fervently to the heart of Jesus to move the hearts of good people to help the work of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate.

  3. Only he can, because he must work for this Work of his Grandmother, since it belongs to his Eternal Father.3 My Jesus, what should matter more to you than this Work, if not that your Father be glorified? These poor creatures, the Daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate, have him constantly on their lips and call on him in all their actions; they hold him in their heart because they love him as Father, placing all their good in him; they adore him in his most exalted

dignity and learn every delight in his divinity; in short, you can well say: «They are the true Daughters of my Eternal Father, for they expect everything from him and rest in him alone».4 My Jesus, is this not true? And can your heart be slow to help these creatures in what they need, and especially the one most in need of all, his slave?

  1. What am I saying, my God! The moment I am in is so important — what a great worry fills my mind. Patience! God be blessed in all things.

  2. Pray, pray, press the dear Heart hard. I always keep you in mind wherever I go; I always carry all my blessed daughters with me, and especially the Superiors, whom I commend to God every day that he may give them light to direct their communities well.5

Goodbye, I am your Poor

Mother [Rosa Gattorno]

God bless you all, and one day may the God who was so favourable to you here on earth be merciful to you in heaven.6

1 The letter she is answering is missing.

2 Her dominant thought at this time is the very purpose of her journey: to obtain recognition of the Institute. But she is also worried about the communities, so she would like to settle the Institute's business in Rome quickly and return, which was not easy. Hence the need for constant, trusting prayer to the Sacred Heart in this month dedicated to him.

3 Belonging to the Eternal Father. It was he who willed it in the Church as the Family of Saint Anne, Jesus' grandmother.

4 This beautiful prayer to Jesus is permeated with the spirit of Trinitarian devotion expressed in the 1869 Rule, Ch. 13, 1-2.

5 The Superiors: Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Mother House, Piacenza; Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, school-infirmary house, Piacenza; Sr. A. Concetta Vernengo, orphanage, Sampierdarena; Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, nurses' house, Genoa.

6 Her orientation towards the fulfilment of life in God is always present and constantly recalled to her Daughters.

If prayer does not miraculously obtain what we want, the horizon looks dark, but the Father's right hand can scatter everything, and the Daughters of Saint Anne will be able to carry the light of faith to the whole world. She longs to return within the walls of Saint Anne's house. She asks for prayers.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. I hope you have received all our letters. My blessed daughter, if prayer does not miraculously obtain what we want, this horizon looks very dark for us;1 but the right hand of our Eternal Father can scatter everything in an instant, and the Daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate, may enjoy the most beautiful light in all Catholicism and make it shine in the most idolatrous lands and plant there the standard of Saint Anne.2

  2. I am glad to hear the good news you give me of the little girls; I bless God for it, asking him to continue pouring on them the dew of his mercies; pray and have others pray.

  3. I am fairly well, only I find myself away from our centre.3 What a different way of living! I always feel I must go and see — what? The dear walls of the Daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate. A hole, even the smallest and narrowest, but in your house, my dear Mother.4

■Hfl

  1. Goodbye; the Lord bless you, and may his gifts be so abundant that they console and sanctify you. And the same for all the others; please read them this line.

  2. Our dear Daughters, pray and storm the heart of Jesus so that this poor Mother of yours may soon obtain everything; so far I have done nothing; how painful it is for me to be outside the walls of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate! Pray, for these are very sad times.

Goodbye; the Lord pour out on you his choicest blessings. I am your

Poor and affectionate Mother Rosa

1 The horizon was indeed dark. Approval of the Institute depended on examination of the 1869 Rule by the S. Congregation of Bishops and Regulars, a task requiring careful thought and a long time. One also had to bear in mind the critical historical relations between the Italian State and the Church and the difficult general situation of ecclesiastical and religious institutions, against which the Italian Government had passed the suppression laws of 1866 and 1870. Cf. L 108, n. 4.

2 Beyond human events Mother Rosa saw God's providential action in his Work, destined to spread «the most beautiful light of faith in the most idolatrous lands» and plant there the banners of Saint Anne.

3 Away from the welcoming and orderly «centre» of the community.

4 She feels out of place in a lay household. The Mother wanted a house in Rome, however tiny. Cf. L 56, n. 2. Looking for it, she feels she is going to see the dear walls of the Daughters of Saint Anne. Her longing becomes a filial prayer to her «Dear Mother» Saint Anne.

-

She has learned from her letter the amount of the debt and is greatly worried. She will leave Rome in five days. A French Religious will arrive in Piacenza; she is to welcome her with every courtesy and tell her of the Mother's imminent return.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter,

  1. I received your last letter, in which I found the figures of everything you owe.1 What can we do? Pray, pray; and as for me, God alone knows the pain and anguish I feel; last night when it reached me it was late, and I assure you it gave me no more rest, with the miller always before me.2 What pain, what sorrow, my God!

  2. Here I have been able to get nothing, or practically nothing, for it is very little; alms are no longer to be found.

  3. Now, God willing, we finally leave Rome on Wednesday evening at 9, and I cannot fix the time of our arrival because I must stop in Bologna, but I will telegraph you on the way or from Bologna.3

  4. Listen, on Wednesday a Religious is to come who is not dressed as a Religious; she is French.4 As soon as you receive this, tell the portress to let her in the moment she arrives and say nothing about whether we are in or not; let her call you, and you will tell her at once: I have received letters from the Mother saying Your Reverence was to come, and since the Mother could not leave Rome until Wednesday, she wrote to me to keep you here until

she arrives. The Mother hopes to be here on Friday morning at the latest.5

  1. Show her every kindness, and for sleeping I would like you to put her in the Teacher's room, asking the Teacher to move wherever you think best, even for the moment into the room where the nurses have their lessons;6 and let the guest room be thoroughly clean. I hope you have had the piano taken away, as it was useless.

  2. So this Religious will stay with you in the Teacher's room; see that she does not leave. If you can't understand her, call Sr. A. Angiola;7 have prayers said that I may arrive alive and that the return journey may not be as painful as the journey here, for I really did not think I would make it.8

I am your most affectionate M. R. God bless you and all the others.

7. Greet everyone for me, and the Delegate9 in particular; tell her I am not writing to her because there is no point, we shall see each other soon.

1 The content of Adelaide's letter, which has not survived, can be inferred from M. Rosa's reply.

2 The debt was evidently large, and the creditors, the miller first and foremost, were pressing. How to remedy it? First of all by prayer, to which she joined her anguish, so keen that it robbed her of sleep.

3 Wednesday evening, the 7th. Although she had fixed the day and route, she had to stay in Rome.

4 A French religious was to arrive the same day, the 7th. She is certainly her friend Soeur de S. Grégoire, whose correspondence survives. Cf. AFSA Pos. Friends.

5 She would have arrived on the 9th because of her stop in Bologna with Countess Maria Anna Trotti.

6 Every day the nurses were given practical lessons on their home nursing service.

7 If you don't understand French, call Sr. A. Angiola Degrossi.

8 It is well known that the Mother suffered greatly when travelling.

9 The Superior of the second house in Piacenza: Sr. A. Francesca Camisa.

She tells him simply that the author of the Rule is Fr. Giovanni Battista Tornatore, to whom she turned after a vision. She begs that the Father be allowed to act freely in the Institute.

Most Holy Father,

  1. For fifteen years, at God's command, I have increased my bodily austerities with the most agonising penances; my food is herbs or pulses; most of these penances are for the Church; Jesus taught me all the instruments he wanted me to use. Now I am most cruelly distressed by a strong fear that they will take my life, or that I shall no longer be able to work in the Lord's work; I am seized by violent attacks that bring me to the point of death; the last time, God commanded me to write to Your Holiness, and I would find relief.

  2. The Rule I presented to Your Holiness was not written by me; while I was praying in the Chapel, Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, appeared to me, and the Servant of God Father Bernardo Maria Clausi told me to go to Mr. Tornatore, Missionary, who would give me the book of our Constitutions. Three times I resisted obeying this command, but the third time I was threatened, and then I obeyed. He is therefore our Founder; he has been working for five years; now the houses are increasing and I, weakened, can barely stand.

  3. I would need a line from Your Holiness so that this Missionary, without diminishing his vocation in the least, could act freely in this work.2

Most Holy Father, deeply prostrate at your most holy Feet, I implore the longed-for grace.

Sr. Anna Maria Rosa Gattorno

1 The Mother was received in private audience by the Holy Father on Sunday 4 June 1871, as Fr. Tornatore wrote to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni. She handed him some «papers», among which this letter is assumed to have been. Cf. Letter of Count Domenico Tellarini to M. Rosa of 10 June 1871, AFSA, 2, 71.

2 On this request, which was very close to her heart, cf. L 5; 12, n. 2; 6, n. 3; 42.

If Providence does not come, it is because Jesus likes to be asked. The month of June favours meditation and contemplation of the Sacred Heart.

A.M.F.

My dear daughter,

  1. I hear Providence is making you sigh; do you know why? It wants us to pray more and more, and our dear Jesus likes to be asked.2

  2. Daughter, what a beautiful month! There is no need even to read the point for meditation, with the Heart of Jesus open. There, there, my dear, take your mind and heart; there you will find everything and rest sweetly.

Goodbye, the Lord bless you all; I am your

P. M. Rosa

1 This is an addition to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino's letter giving news of the Mother, her activities and her visits to the Cardinals.

2 A few words, but full of affection, on the key points of daily life: poverty of means, the constant search for Jesus, source of every material and spiritual good and fulfilment of all our desires.

She asks him to intercede with the Holy Father to reply to a note of hers.

Most Reverend Eminence,

  1. I beg Your Most Reverend Eminence to have the charity to set my mind at rest about my fear of not obtaining from His Holiness what I desire. Your Eminence alone can obtain everything for me in answer to the little note I handed His Holiness.3

  2. I ask Your Most Reverend Eminence to hear one who, deeply humbled at your feet, awaits the Apostolic Blessing, as she signs herself with the greatest veneration

Your Most Reverend Eminence's

most humble, most obedient Servant Sr. Anna

Maria Rosa Gattorno

1 The recipient's name is missing in M. Rosa's autograph letter. He is certainly the Cardinal Vicar, as appears from a letter on the matter written to her by his secretary Fr. Domenico Tellarini on 10 June 1871.

2 The date too is deduced from the latter.

3 In that letter, after telling her of the Cardinal's interest, he adds: «Among the papers you handed him the Holy Father found only a small card containing the summary of the Rule, and this too he passed on to the Congregation of Bishops and Regulars, without showing the least reluctance towards your petitions».

She encloses a letter for the Princess and asks her to deliver it. They have received the Holy Father's blessing and she will be able to bring her a Crucifix he has blessed. Courage; the Lord will soon console her.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter,

  1. I have just received two lines from you, forwarded from Piacenza with Sr. A. Serafina's. I enclose a letter for Maria, the Princess.2 Send it at once to Sr. A. Serafina.

  2. Courage; the Holy Father blessed us, and you will also have a crucifix blessed by the Holy Father.3

  3. Pray. Goodbye. I am glad to hear the Sister is better. Blessed be God, who knows how to do everything for our good. Yes, my blessed daughter, you will see that the Lord will soon console you.

  4. Meanwhile, for vegetables and potatoes, tell Sr. A. Serafina to go and get them from the gardener at S. P. d'Arena, and I will see to it afterwards; indeed you can have as many potatoes fetched as you like. God bless you.

In haste, your poor

Mother Rosa

1 The date is presumed from the context.

2 Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi was at the Genoa house. Princess Maria d'Annenkoff lived in Genoa.

3 She had had the audience with the Holy Father on 4 June 1871.

She should have much prayer offered to the Sacred Heart of Jesus and seek strength and consolation in him, and she will be heard. She should urge one Sister to be prudent in speech and point out to another her fault against the Rule.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter, wholly ours

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. A few hours ago I received your last letter, dated the 3rd, and I also received all the others you mention in it.2

  2. My dear, have much prayer offered to this dear Heart of Jesus — what a sweet month! — the Heart of Jesus that receives our every poor sigh; so, my beloved, take everything to this heart, go and get everything from this heart, and you will find everything. Say to him: «Dear Jesus, let me too taste just one little drop of your sweetest nectar», and you will see that Jesus will give you everything, because he wants to hear us seek it and to give it to those who truly long for it with faith and openness.3 God gives this to the simple and not to the wise of this world.4

  3. Everything you write me is fine; I am delighted with what you tell me about the Heart of Jesus, and I bless God.

  4. Silence, for charity's sake; impose silence on Sister Sr. A. Felicita — silence.5 You are also right about Sr. A. del Buon Pastore, who did not do well; call her and tell her: «My daughter,

listen, without realising it you broke a rule, because you should not have revealed to your sister what you had received in church, but should have come only to me. So from now on please do not do it again», and then you will hear what she says. You will answer: «The Mother and the Father will soon come, and you can tell them everything».6

Goodbye, my dear; the Lord bless you and all the others; I am your

Affectionate Mother Rosa

1 From the context it can be assigned to this period.

2 None of these letters has survived.

3 With simple but profound ideas she expresses her «spirituality of the Sacred Heart», drawn not from books but from experience: the Heart of Christ, a human-divine heart, close, accessible, open. It receives everything, gives everything. From it flows eternally intoxicating love, «sweetest nectar», for whoever seeks and longs for it with faith and limpid sincerity.

4 This is a gift God grants to the little ones. Cf. Lk 10:21.

5 Sr. A. Felicita Grisleri.

6 Sr. A. del Buon Pastore Bastia. She even suggests the words to use in case she is not convinced. You broke a rule: Ch. 9, p. 90, Rule of 1869.

She shares in her sufferings. She should try to obtain free baths for the girl with scrofula. She answers her questions, advising how to act. She should make a novena to St Joseph.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. Yesterday I received your letter and hear of all your troubles; at once I asked the Lord to transfer them onto my shoulders, for my chest already shares the pain.1

  2. My God, how cruel the news of the poor little girl was to me!2 Patience; you should get the Doctor to write a certificate showing that she needs baths, and then go to Monsignor's Chaplain to see whether he can get her sent to the baths, as Count Caracciolo did; and the certificate should say she has scrofula; but do it at once.

  3. For taking the boys to confession you can send two religious, but [accompanied] by the Teacher; choose those who seem most capable to you.3

  4. As for work, I have just received letters from the Delegate of S. P. d'Arena, who is sending some, and then the Delegate of the Dal Verme House can give you some.4

  5. As for adoration, do what you can; God is content at once when we do what we can; so let us do everything with holy simplicity, love God the Father very much and try

to obtain everything from him. He is all patience and meekness, all Charity and love; and our holy Mother Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate, was adorned with these virtues.5

  1. Make a novena to St Joseph and say to him: hear us, dear support of the Daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate; and you will see that providence will come; but don't bully the saints; pray to them with patience and resignation.6

  2. Goodbye, my dear daughter; the Lord bless you and make you holy. Greet them all for me and tell them I wish them the choicest blessings from Heaven that a creature can share.

Goodbye; I am your Poor Mother Rosa

1 Her empathy with Sr. A. Francesca is particularly deep.

2 Cf. L 50, n. 5.

3 The schoolboys were taken to the nearby parish of «S. Maria dei Pagani».

4 The Delegate Sr. A. Concetta Vernengo was sending to Piacenza work commissioned by a merchant, namely shirt-making. Cf. letter of Sr. A. Concetta Vernengo to M. Rosa of 19 July 1871. AFSA, D 1.

5 Not an abstract God: it is the Father revealing himself in the face of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate.

6 With the gospel attitude of humility. Cf. Lk 18:13-14.

She should give precise information about Sr. A. Ernesta. Courage: trials are needed to progress in holiness. From meditation on the poverty of Bethlehem and Nazareth she will draw «every delight».

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. I have [just] received another letter from you, and one yesterday, telling me about Sister Sr. A. Ernesta. I cannot make out which one she is: the cook or the other one who arrived with Sr. A. Santina's sister?1 When you answer, please tell me clearly who she is, so that I can understand.

  2. I also hear about this one's unease; try to see where all her bad behaviour comes from, and then we will think about it.2 As for the other matter you mention, be patient; everything will be settled. I will come very soon; for now I am too busy here and cannot move, but I do not stop writing and thinking to get a little corner for you.3

  3. Do you see that the moment of suffering I spoke of has come? But would it not have been to be feared that it was not the Lord's will for these Religious to live in Genoa?4 So courage, for the moment of trial is necessary; courage and patience, peace, resignation; with these everything is obtained and every obstacle overcome.5

  4. What shall I say to the Daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate? Only that in time of trial great strides are made on the way of holiness, and our soul is adorned with virtues and grows great, and finally, when peace returns, enjoys its fruit, sharing in the delights of its beloved Jesus.

  5. Courage: your tribulations are few compared with the house of Nazareth, which lacked everything, and in it lived the three richest personages of Heaven; there was no bed, only straw, in the Hut at Bethlehem, and yet the Son of God chose it as his first dwelling and willed to be born there; the Queen of Heaven and earth seated where? On straw, beside a manger, feeding only on the beautiful light of Jesus. In him she found everything: the comforts and delights of the world; everything was contained in that dear Child.6

  6. And you, who can look at him within your heart, will find every delight if you keep your gaze on him alone. Blessed be God always, who deigns to lower his most holy hand.

Goodbye; be ever the blessed ones in your tribulations.7 I am

Your Poor Mother Rosa

1 Sr. A. Ernesta Savani had received the religious habit on 16 April 1871. She cannot quite identify her. Sr. A. Santina's sister was a postulant.

2 The unease, that is, her basically wrong attitude, shown in her refusal to accept community norms. The Mother wants the roots of her unhappiness and bad behaviour to be understood.

3 She continues to work and worry so that they might have suitable premises for the community.

4 The moment of suffering she had warned them of has come. Without that «suffering», how much there would have been to fear that it was not the Lord's will for the Sisters to live in Genoa!

5 The moment of trial is necessary. Here is the reason for the positive side of trial. It engages them in practising the virtues (= values) that accompany fortitude: courage, energy deployed to overcome difficulties; patience, strength to resist the sadness that would weaken and dishearten; peace, self-control and balance in adversity; resignation, the strength of goodness shown in powerlessness — «I send you out as lambs among wolves», says Jesus — with readiness to fall, if it comes to that, while patiently resisting for the sake of the good and fighting for it.

6 Courage... after her pointed reminder that trial is needed for full human and Christian growth, the Mother adds, as a further invitation to accept and live courageously the hardships of poverty, the teaching of the «three richest personages of heaven». Contemplating the house of Nazareth and the hut

of Bethlehem is a source of knowledge of the value of poverty and a sure path to the irrevocable choice of Jesus: only delight.

7 Conclusion: we must therefore bless God, who deigns to lower his most holy hand by permitting suffering. In tribulations lies the beatitude of blessing.

She suggests how to deal with a difficult sister. She is eager to return soon among her daughters; it is hard to live outside the walls of the religious house, but she is also convinced that eternal life in Paradise must be earned. There are the first four sisters, who form Saint Anne's retinue. She is consoled and strengthened by the thought that none of her daughters will die without obtaining salvation.

I hear that Signora Caterina gave you F 30. Poor dear, she is clearly always thinking of you.6

  1. Daughters, pray that I may soon be done,7 for these days, I assure you, I am in the greatest distress, and everything is getting so complicated that only prayer can open the way and free us from so many anxieties.

  2. My little brain works night and day, and the anxiety I feel is very strong, seeing myself in someone else's house, and thinking of you, and seeing myself held captive — and who knows for how much longer!

  3. Oh, my daughters, believe me, many times Sr. A. Vincenza and I do long for a little corner in our own house, together with our Sisters, for here everyone watches us,8 and so often we have to bear great hardship because we cannot even have water. Do you see, my dears, what it costs to be outside our walls?

  4. Ah, daughters, believe me, we do not reach paradise unless we have first earned eternal life with toil. Up there everything is over. The Daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate, will have an eminent place near the Mother of the Immaculate, as the four who had the good fortune to enter into rest there already form her retinue.10

  5. None will die without being saved and being sure of Paradise, with little Purgatory. This thought alone, believe me, is enough to give me strength and courage to face any torment whatever, any persecution, because everything fades before this most beautiful horizon.11 What is a torment caused by men compared with the lovely caresses Jesus will give us?

I close because it is very late and my health is poor, as usual.

God bless you and make you happy. Goodbye; I am your

poor Mother S. A. M. Rosa

1 The date follows from a letter of Fr Tornatore of 13 June 1871 to the Superior Paola Bucciotti about Sr. A. Ernesta's faults and how to deal with her. Since M. Rosa says below, «Tomorrow I will speak to the Father about it and I hope he will write himself», this letter is evidently of 12 June.

2 Cf. previous L (69) 1-2 and the relevant notes.

3 They are let pass, such faults are tolerated; it cannot be avoided that they suffer from the bad example.

4 Once one fault has been corrected and amended, you will take up another, and the evil will be removed.

5 The Father, informed, wrote the same day: 13 June 1871 (cf. AFSA, 1).

6 Signora Caterina Rusca, the landlady.

7 That she may finish soon. Everything is getting complicated. The Holy Father had had the Rule and other documents sent to the S. Congregation of Bishops and Regulars, the Dicastery competent for examination and judgement. The matter therefore could not be settled at once. Cf. L 65, n. 3.

8 We are under everyone's eyes.

9 The reasons for discomfort are many, but in every painful situation she finds the gospel side: the Kingdom of heaven suffers violence (Mt 11:12).

10 The first four Sisters to die:

  • Sr. A. Daria Vagni, died at Cento on 22.8.1867;

  • Sr. A. Blandina Grossi, died at Sampierdarena on 15.2.1870;

  • Sr. A. Crocifissa Dugoni, died at Sampierdarena on 30.7.1870;

  • Sr. A. Benedetta Stabelini, died at Piacenza on 6.11.1870.

Most Holy Father,

  1. The undersigned Petitioner, prostrate at the most holy feet of Your Beatitude, humbly sets forth that she is at the head of the Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate Virgin and Mother of God, founded five years ago.2

  2. The purpose of the said Institute is to honour the Saint's privilege of being Mother of the Immaculate.

  3. Its primary works for the neighbour are home nursing of the sick of both sexes, by day and by night, and taking in girls at risk to safeguard their innocence.

  4. With the permission of the respective Ordinaries four houses have been founded: two in Piacenza, the third in S. P. D'Arena and the fourth in Genoa.

  5. The Religious number about 80; the girls at risk they have taken in number about 120, all so far relying on Divine Providence.3

  6. The Petitioner humbly asks a special blessing on herself and her Religious, and a word of approval from You, so as to be sure that the Institute is a plant of the heavenly Father and to be encouraged to continue the work.

  7. To present her petition, the Petitioner takes the occasion of the solemn privilege the Immaculate grants to Your Holiness's Pontificate, namely that of completing its twenty-fifth year.

  2. Now you may think that here we are enjoying feasts and ceremonies of the Holy Father. Daughter, quite the opposite. I can tell you that Rome is pitiful to see: all Christians live as if in prison; no one can shout a «viva» without being put in prison at once. The Holy Father is always imprisoned.2 The delegations that come are booed by ruffians. In short, everything comes down to prayers and penances: processions of women and of men, and prayers in the churches, in silence. One cannot go out, for every moment they stone the Priests; they hold demonstrations against the nuns. The Jews make tremendous uproars, and we are obliged to

But let everything be for the greater glory of our Eternal Father; to him everything, and to us the misery of Adam.

  2. If by chance you find yourselves with nothing, turn to Sig. Brigidini to advance you two hundred francs, or in my name, and you can share some of it with the Delegate of the Morte.6

  3. You mention the little girls in the garden: provided they are with you and well supervised, you may take them.

  4. Have you still given nothing to the pharmacist? You ask whether you should give the 400 f. to the miller; you may, but where did you give the F. 600? Have you paid all the small bills? Try, if you can, to give something to the pharmacist; and always send something to those of the Morte.7

  5. How it pained me to hear about the soup. Patience! What can we do? Pray, and I assure you I pray always, and more so here, where we are always alone and I go out8 only on the House's business and nothing else. Then I had a cruel night, and so the next day I stayed in bed all day.

  2. Imagine: my only consolation was reading your letters, and hearing that our poor houses are going well consoled me and encouraged me to be strong. Yes, my dear, my only consolation is to hear that you faithfully observe your holy Rule.1

  3. My daughter, believe this poor mother of yours: if the Rule is observed in your Houses,2 you will never lack

providence; on the contrary, the choicest and most abundant blessings will be poured out on you, as I wish them for you with all my soul.

  1. Patience and suffering are the two great points on which our holiness and eternal happiness rest: brief suffering for great joy.3

  2. I did not quite understand what you want me to send you, but I am expecting Sr. A. Vincenza, who will explain better, and I will send you whatever you want. For charity's sake take care of yourself; don't wear yourself out; let the strong ones do the running and you direct — that is enough.

  3. I also hear the good news about the kind Ladies,4 and about the Mayor, who is entirely well disposed towards you; so let us hope. I close because it is late and I am not very well.

Goodbye; I am your Poor

Affectionate Mother Rosa Gattorno

1 Observant of your Rule of life. Doing what accords with the spirit and the letter of the rule.

2 If in your two communities (Sampierdarena and Genoa) — cf. L 87, n. 3 — the Rule is observed, that is, if they live in docility, obedience, self-denial and the desire to become true Daughters of Saint Anne, the sign of God's blessing will not be lacking: providence.

3 Patience and suffering. Patience is the strength of Christ's passivity, who accepted suffering and made the joy of new life spring from it. To follow him on the way of suffering in life's brief span is a sure guarantee of immense, eternal joy.

She explains that her silence was due to poor health. He should drive away as a temptation of the devil the thought of losing interest in the Daughters of Saint Anne. Rather, he should do his best to bring them to Rome. She is preparing the religious for the new house in Ferrara.

A.M.F.

Good Father Agostino,

  1. I have just received your letter full of complaints. Why do you act like this? Listen: for 15 days I had excruciating pains in my head and cheek, and it was impossible for me to write. I could barely do the bare minimum; but Carlotta and Sr. A. Vincenza wrote to you at length.

  2. It is only three days, counting today, since these dear friends left me. Believe me, the work of this institute is killing me, so many and so varied are its demands. So be it; I will do everything for our God, for his greater glory.

  3. Father Agostino, why do you say you no longer want to concern yourself with the poor daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate? Why let yourself be seized by those ugly thoughts — that someone has forbidden me to write to you? Come now! It is truly cepinetto at work. Nothing should surprise us now that it is Cepinetto's great carnival season.1

  4. That ugly monster works, and we must stay quiet, shut up in the heart of God the Father, consoling ourselves and mocking him and his ugly tail. A disgusting creature, a real kitchen rag.

  5. You, Father Agostino, say you don't want to think about the Daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate. Listen: on the contrary, you must do every-

thing to have them come and occupy Rome soon;2 then we shall be near you and you will have no more fears.

  1. I had a letter from Father Manfredini.3 He knows nothing about our Rule. The Count writes that all is going well, and also that Svegliati has died.4 Father Agostino, have you sent all your novices away? You will be free and able to travel more easily.

  2. The Countess is having work done in Ferrara.5 I am preparing the Religious. Sr. A. Vincenza is at S. P. D'Arena on my behalf, but will soon be back here. Father Agostino, don't say the Daughters of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate, [have forgotten you], for your name comes up all the time, and all those you sent greetings to return them.

In haste, bless me, and believe me always your

Poor Sr. Anna Maria Rosa Gattorno

3 Father Giuseppe Manfredini SJ.

She has learnt that the uncle is not well disposed towards the Sisters, and asks her to explain everything to her mother. She should take it all calmly, accepting the cross, which unites to Jesus as a reward at the last hour. She should pray for her uncle, as the Mother does.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter, wholly mine for all ages

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. I have just received a letter from Sr. A. Serafina in which she tells me all that your uncle said to her.1 Listen, my daughter: first you must take it all calmly and commend yourself to the Lord, and then send for your mother and tell her kindly: «Dear mamma, please tell uncle that he could have used other means of dealing with my sisters, but never mind. He wants to speak with me, and I don't think it right to start arguing with a man». Tell her only this: «I can testify that my Mother has never spoken of him, either in Rome or elsewhere, for he never comes to her mind; his bad conduct towards our house grieves me not a little».2 Tell your Mother everything and say: «What does he want to tell Monsignor? Let him say what he likes; truth always carries the day; and let him rest assured that no one will go and disturb him, and they won't go there any more. Give him my regards».3

  2. And you, my dear daughter, don't be upset; take it all calmly and be cheerful; hurry, so that you can come back to me. Carlotta longs for you.

  3. God wants us on the cross; very well, let us settle ourselves comfortably on it, so that when we die we shall have near us our dear Jesus, our only Love, the Being of our life.4

  4. My daughter, I am writing to you from the Morte, where I am waiting for the Father5 to come and clothe Paola, who will then at once take the post of teacher; today I thought I would have letters from you, but I received only Sr. A. Serafina's, with these fine things in it.

  5. You can add that your uncle should know the Mother has relatives who will see that she is respected, and he should take care not to end up having to repent in Rome, for the Mother will keep silent as long as order does not suffer, but then she will do what she must. After all he did to me, does he still have the nerve to talk like this? God is with us, and he will have to think very carefully.6

  6. If by the time you receive this you have already been there, I hope you answered with charity whatever the Lord inspired you to say. I want you to hurry.

  7. Only yesterday I received half a sheet from you along with the M. Delegate's, and this is the 4th letter I have written you — the fifth, I think, counting a little sheet I put inside the Delegate's.7 So you see? After lunch I will send to the Post again. Goodbye; be cheerful and, for charity's sake, don't grow melancholy over these things. Pray for your uncle, as does this your8

Affectionate Mother Rosa

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

Good Father Agostino,

  1. She has received his letter. She can tell him only of afflictions, yet she gladly stays on Golgotha suffering with the dear Redeemer. It is sweet to receive the blows of creatures held close to Jesus. From his wounds he draws the sweetness to console every pain.

A.M.F.

Good Father Agostino,

  1. I have received your letter, my Father Agostino; what am I to say in reply? What news can I give you, when I have nothing but afflictions to tell?1 My God! Pain upon pain. Always dying and never dying, always a martyr and never martyrdom; so, my Father Agostino, are you not tired of receiving letters full of anguish and affliction? Will you come with me to Golgotha? Yes, my Father Agostino, gladly, together on this dear mountain, to rejoice in the suffering of our dear Redeemer.2

  2. We shall beg him to rest, making him an uncomfortable bed of our poor breast; and we on the cross drinking in every kind of pain and sorrow — especially I, a most infamous creature, who have caused him so many pains and keep on causing them.

  3. Today, the day of dear Mary under the sweetest title of the Rosary,3 she gave me such a gift, so sweetly, that I spent the whole day clinging to the most holy feet of Jesus. Inside those most holy holes, for had I been outside I would have died, so many were the thrusts of every kind I had to receive.4
